title: Test consistency with PROJ's +proj=healpix projection
body:
PROJ implements ellipsoidal HEALPix as `+proj=healpix` (geodetic → authalic latitude → HPX projection), the same construction healpix-geo uses. This adds tests that the two agree, so the projection can be relied on as a CRS for healpix-geo data (e.g. in GeoTIFF) and any future drift is caught.

`tests/test_proj.py` projects cell vertices from `nested.vertices` with PROJ and checks that:

- every cell is a square of the expected size on the plane, for depths 0, 1 and 3, `lon_0` 0° and 90°, and the `unitsphere`, `sphere`, `WGS84` and `GRS80` ellipsoids. A further test checks that `lon_0=45°` does *not* line up with the cells;
- every pair of edge neighbours (depth 3) shares its edge. The only exception is the pairs across the cuts between polar triangles: they share a meridian on the globe but lie in separate triangles on the plane, and the test checks this too;
- PROJ's inverse of each square's centre gives back the same cell through `lonlat_to_healpix` (depth 4).

HEALPix is an interrupted projection, so a vertex that lies exactly on a cut (a pole, a polar facet boundary or the map edge) has no unique image. Each vertex is therefore moved 1e-7 of the way towards its own cell centre before it is projected, which puts the whole cell on its own facet. PROJ parameters come from `ellipsoid.resolve`, so the two libraries use the same ellipsoid.

`pyproj` is added to the `tests` pixi feature. The module uses `pytest.importorskip("pyproj")`, so it is skipped where pyproj is unavailable.

Checked locally against healpix-geo 0.4.1 / PROJ 9.9.0: 33 passed. The tests also fail as expected if the nudge is removed (24 failures), if PROJ uses a different ellipsoid (14), or if the neighbour IDs are wrong (4). ruff and black pass.

Background and figures: https://github.com/GRID4EARTH/healpix-proj
